iFinder (Lin et al., "Understanding Implicit Trust Errors in Core Carrier Networks through
Multi-Agent Flaw Discovery and Analysis", USENIX Security 2026; arXiv 2607.10315v2)
-- 22 ground-truth GitHub security issues
=======================================================================================
SOURCE NOTE: The paper does NOT list the 22 issues; it only says (Sec. 3) "we gathered 22 security
issues from two widely used open-source CN implementations, Open5GS and free5GC" and evaluates
recall on them (Table 1: iFinder TP 15 / FN 7; EA built valid PoCs for 19/22).
The list below is from the paper's official artifact (Open Science section):
https://zenodo.org/records/20534406  -> iFinder_artifact-v4.tar.gz -> dataset/README.md
(downloaded 2026-11-06). Titles/state/date from the GitHub API, 2026-11-06.

All 22 are PFCP (N4) bugs; 20 in the UPF, 2 in the SMF; 17 open5gs + 5 free5gc entries.
They map to 19 distinct GitHub URLs: open5gs#3207 ("Some assertions can be triggered") backs
4 entries (005, 010, 011, 013); open5gs#3040 is a pull request (fix), not an issue.
Oracle: crash (EA "only checks whether a PoC produces the expected runtime effect, which in the
case of an FP, is always a crash").
Patterns: PA = syntactic validation missing, PB = semantic invariant missing, PC = resource
availability not checked.

id | repo/issue | NF | CWE | pattern | GitHub title | state | opened

Distinct URLs: open5gs#2127, #2128, #2523, #3040(PR), #3207, #3574, #3642, #3727, #3747, #3839, #3840, #3841, #3847, #3964; free5gc#17, #482, #483, #496, #746
Note (judged from titles only): none of the 22 is an NF-restart / PFCP-association-recovery bug; all are crafted/malformed-input or resource-exhaustion crashes.
